name: Freshworks
task: A help desk, tickets or a shared inbox
summary: Suite of separately-sold products: Freshdesk support, Freshservice IT, Freshsales CRM, Freshchat and Freshcaller.
best_for: teams who want a support desk that is cheaper per agent than the category leaders and will genuinely use the annual commitment — Growth at $19 is real value if ticketing is all you need
skip_if: you want the AI-first product the marketing describes without doing the arithmetic, because that configuration is $55 plus $29 an agent annually, or $66 plus $35 if you take the monthly column
honest_knock: Freshworks is not a product, it is nine of them behind a pricing page that contains no price. Once you find Freshdesk's own page, two things sit on top of the number. Freddy AI Copilot — the AI the marketing leads with — is $29 per agent per month extra, 53% on top of a Pro seat, and it is not sold on Growth at all. And the Freddy AI Agent that is included stops after 500 sessions; beyond that it is $49 per 100 sessions, so a busy queue turns the included allowance into a metered bill. The SAVE 20% badge on the annual toggle is really 17%. If you want support and IT and CRM, price three subscriptions, not one. In our Freshdesk test on 21 October 2026 a new account's time zone was not set to Amsterdam despite the EU data centre, so ticket times were hours off until you change it.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Freshdesk Growth · per agent per month billed annually
pricing.notes: (2026-08-29, read on their own pricing pages) The main Freshworks pricing page still carries no prices at all — it lists the products and links out to each one, and that list has grown to nine: Freshdesk Omni, Freshdesk, Freshchat, Freshcaller, Freshservice, Freshservice for Business Teams, Freshsales, Freshsales Suite and Freshmarketer. On Freshdesk the annual rates are unchanged since 1 August 2026: Growth $19 per agent per month, Pro $55, Enterprise $89, billed annually. What has changed is that the monthly column is now published: Growth $23, Pro $66, Enterprise $107 per agent per month, billed monthly. The page's SAVE 20% badge overstates the gap — $19 against $23 is 17.4%, $55 against $66 is 16.7%, $89 against $107 is 16.8%. Freddy AI Agent is included with the first 500 sessions; additional sessions are $49 per 100. Freddy AI Copilot is a separate add-on at $29 per agent per month annually, or $35 monthly, on Pro and Enterprise only. Day passes are $2, $7 and $12 per pass on Growth, Pro and Enterprise. Connector app tasks are $80 per 5,000 tasks. The 14-day free trial starts you on Enterprise (in our test on 21 October 2026 the sign-up page promised a '14-day all-access free trial' and the app then said 'your 15-day trial starts today'). Re-verified 11 October 2026 on freshworks.com/freshdesk/pricing/: the annual rates ($19, $55, $89), the $29 Copilot add-on, the $49 per 100 extra AI Agent sessions, the $2/$7/$12 day passes and the $80 per 5,000 connector tasks are unchanged, and a new add-on is listed on every tier: MCP actions at $15 per 1,000. The monthly column is not in the page source we read, so the monthly figures above date from 29 August 2026. The FAQ on the same page adds that the 500 free AI Agent sessions are given once per account, not every month; that an email AI Agent session is a 72-hour window from the customer's first email; that purchased session packs expire with your payment cycle; and that downgrades and cancellations take effect only at the end of your term.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on Freshdesk, during the trial that starts with a new account (Freshdesk Omni, EU data centre), without connecting a channel, a mailbox or an integration: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We created three tickets with known priorities and statuses, changed one and added a private note.
findings: The sign-up page promised a '14-day all-access free trial'; inside the app the banner said 'your 15-day trial starts today', next to a 'Buy now' button. Our own company domain was accepted without a business-email check.

All three tickets (#4, #5 and #6) were created with a 'Ticket created' message, and in All tickets all nine values we set (subject, priority and status) were right. The open Low-priority ticket got a deadline straight away: 'First response due in 7 hours'.

Times were off by default: tickets created on the evening of 21 October, Amsterdam time, showed as 'Thu, 22 Oct 2026 at 3:24 AM'. The new account's time zone was not Amsterdam, despite the EU data centre. It can be changed; we did not check whether SLA deadlines move with it.

Onboarding asked for industry, experience, up to three goals and support channels, then offered 'Build your first AI Agent' from a website, with 'Skip for now'; we skipped it. The workspace already held three sample tickets with sample contacts.
The New ticket form sets Source to Phone and Product to 'Example' by default and requires a Description; a 'Create another' box lets you add tickets in a row.
Changing FD-BETA from High to Low in the list view stuck: the opened ticket showed Priority Low and Status Pending. The private note was marked orange, and no email went out.

'Add AI summary' on every ticket, 'Write with AI' in the note editor and the AI Agent builder were all on offer during the trial. We did not click them, and what remains of them after the trial is not established.
